sections.heading: Default structure
sections.text: Half-bridge uses two switches with a split-capacitor voltage divider to generate a bipolar drive voltage. Duty cycle must stay below 0.5 per switch. Peak-current-mode control is preferred for inherent volt-second balancing and overcurrent protection.

sections.heading: Design formulas
sections.text: V_out = D*V_in/(2*N) where N = N_sec/N_pri, D<0.5. The split capacitors must be sized to hold the midpoint voltage within a few percent of V_in/2 under load. Effective output frequency = 2*fsw. Dead time: 50-200ns to prevent shoot-through.

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: The split-capacitor midpoint voltage drifts if the two capacitors are not well matched or if the duty cycles are asymmetric. This causes DC bias in the transformer. Current-mode control with per-switch sensing corrects this automatically. The voltage stress on each switch is V_in (not V_in/2).

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If the half-bridge shows capacitor midpoint drift, verify the current sensing is per-switch. If the switches are overstressed (V_in > switch rating), consider a full-bridge for higher voltage applications. For power > 1kW, full-bridge is typically more efficient.
